subject: Escrowed credits & banded pricing — clarifying invoice/overage handling
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Mendez <jorge.m@acmeretail.com>, procurement <procurement@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Escrowed credits & banded pricing — clarifying invoice/overage handling

Hi Jorge / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — really appreciated the deep dive on your catalog-ingestion throughput. To keep the momentum I wanted to share a couple of clarifying items related to the hosted rate card we discussed and how an escrowed-credit arrangement would work for a banded (tiered) volume commitment. Attached: redwood-hosted-ratecard-v2.pdf.

Quick summary / asks: 
- Can you confirm expected monthly token distribution (approx. % by band) so we can recommend the correct banding?
- Do you prefer monthly invoicing with a true-up, or a monthly prepay model (we can support both for enterprise deals)?
- Are there procurement/legal constraints around holding credits in escrow vs a standard prepaid invoice?

How we typically structure this:
- Banded discounts applied to consumption tiers (example in attachment).
- Committed monthly minimum is invoiced at start of billing period. Unused committed credits roll forward for up to 90 days.
- Escrowed credits: for customers who want funds held by a neutral escrow agent, we can accommodate this for 12+ month commitments; Redwood will draw down credits monthly upon invoice submission.
- Overage: consumption above committed amount is billed at the overage band rate on the following monthly invoice; we can set a monthly cap or automatic throttling if you want hard limits.

If you can share the rough token profile (example: 200M tokens/month baseline, 1B burst for promotions), I’ll ask our sales ops team to produce a sample billing schedule and a DocuSign-ready escrow term sheet.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment(s): redwood-hosted-ratecard-v2.pdf (summary of bands & sample pricing)

From: Jorge Mendez <jorge.m@acmeretail.com>

Thanks Rachel — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions before procurement starts the legal review: 

- Our rough profile: baseline ~250M tokens/month; during 3 major promos/year we expect three-week bursts of ~900M tokens. Is banding applied monthly or per-call?
- If we choose escrowed credits, is there a minimum escrow amount? We prefer not to prepay more than 2 months of expected spend up front.
- Overages: can you confirm whether overages are billed immediately (real-time) or on the following invoice with a grace buffer? We want to avoid surprises for our finance team.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@acmeretail.com) to coordinate PO timing.

Regards,
Jorge Mendez
Head of AI Platform | Acme Retail
jorge.m@acmeretail.com

Subject: Re: Escrowed credits & banded pricing — clarifying invoice/overage handling

Hi Jorge — quick answers and an initial sample schedule below; attached: escrow-terms-draft.docx.

Answers: 
- Banding: discounts are applied monthly based on the month’s total consumption. So if in July you use 1.1B tokens (baseline + burst), billing for July will apply the tiered rates to the 1.1B breakouts.
- Minimum escrow: we typically require a 1-month committed minimum to be funded into escrow for the first draw; subsequent months draw from escrow. For your preference of not prepaying more than 2 months, we can structure a rolling escrow funded monthly with a 30–60 day buffer.
- Overages: we invoice overages on the following monthly invoice (true-up model) by default. If you prefer near-real-time notifications, we can enable monthly usage alerts and an automated cap that stops additional requests once a hard threshold is hit.

Sample banded pricing (illustrative, final numbers subject to legal & finance approval):
- Band A: 0 – 100M tokens/month — $0.025 / 1k tokens
- Band B: 100M – 1B tokens/month — $0.018 / 1k tokens
- Band C: >1B tokens/month — $0.012 / 1k tokens
- Example: if July = 1.1B tokens, billing breaks down by band.

Escrow specifics: 
- Escrow agent: neutral third-party (we use AcmeEscrow Services or your preferred agent).
- Drawdown: Redwood submits monthly invoice; escrow releases funds up to the invoiced amount.
- Refunds/terminations: unused escrowed credits refundable after 90 days less any adjustments for usage.

Next steps I propose: 
1) If OK with banding model, procurement shares PO timeline and any escrow vendor constraints.
2) We’ll produce a DocuSign-ready term sheet for the escrow and a sample invoice schedule showing baseline, burst, and overage scenarios.

I’ve copied Ben (sales lead) and Laura (sales ops) for approval on the illustrative bands and to produce a formal quote.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): escrow-terms-draft.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escrowed credits & banded pricing — clarifying invoice/overage handling

Nice summary Rachel. A couple of negotiation notes for Acme: 
- Recommend we offer a blended prepay rebate for 12-month term: 5% off list if they prepay 6 months, 9% if they prepay 12 months. Escrow option can sit alongside the prepay but reduces rebate to 7% if escrow is used due to third-party fees.
- Consider a burst cushion: include one free burst month at Band C pricing applied as a credit once per 12-month period. Helps close when customers worry about promo events.
- Finance ask: require amortized monthly invoicing for revenue recognition; avoid large single upfront that their accounting won't accept.

I’ll flag to sales director for approval on the free-burst credit and exact rebate percentages, but we can send the DocuSign term sheet with the sample banding and these optional concessions for procurement to review.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
